title: CA 91326: A Public Choice Mystery Investigation - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Alex Tabarrok uses ChatGPT to investigate why a California CPUC clean-energy grant round was limited to organizations headquartered in ZIP 91326, tracing the restriction to a thinly-scrutinized August 2026 budget bill amendment and a network linking Save Porter Ranch's director to legislators. He argues public choice should do more micro-history case studies like this.

insights.claim: On Sept 9, 2026, the California Public Utilities Commission announced clean energy grants open only to eligible organizations headquartered in ZIP Code 91326, money tied to the 2015-16 Aliso Canyon gas leak.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Illustrates how utility penalty funds can be steered via narrow eligibility rules.
insights.quote: for eligible organizations headquartered in ZIP Code 91326

insights.claim: The legislature appropriated $2 million from the Aliso Canyon Recovery Account for outreach across an 11-community disaster area; the first round distributed about $1.3 million competitively, while Round 3 was restricted to a single ZIP code with a $75,000 maximum award and excluded prior recipients.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Shows the contrast between competitive allocation and bespoke earmarks within the same pot.

insights.claim: Save Porter Ranch, headquartered in ZIP 91326 and long active in CPUC Aliso Canyon proceedings, was a conspicuous likely beneficiary of the restriction.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Regulatory proceedings participants can be rewarded through tailored grant design.

insights.claim: The 91326 restriction did not originate with CPUC staff but was inserted by the Legislature into the August 2026 budget cleanup bill.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Earmark risk sits in budget trailer bills, not only in agency discretion.
insights.quote: The 91326 restriction did not originate with CPUC staff. The Legislature itself inserted it into the 2026 budget cleanup bill

insights.claim: Save Porter Ranch director Richard Mathews is president of the North Valley Democratic Club, which counts legislators Schiavo and Gabriel as members or endorsees; Schiavo sits on Budget and Utilities & Energy, and Gabriel chairs Assembly Budget.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Political network mapping reveals how small earmarks get routed.

insights.claim: The amendment moved through a budget-bill junior with a thin record—amended August 28, withdrawn from committee August 30, passed August 31—and floor presentations never mentioned the single-ZIP limit; the Assembly passed it 72-0.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Budget trailer bills are a low-scrutiny channel for localized favors; watch them for regulatory surprises.

insights.claim: The evidence shows how a highly localized legislative earmark can pass with effectively zero scrutiny, though it does not demonstrate corruption, and the decisive evidence of who requested the ZIP language is likely not indexed online.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Distinguishes suggestive circumstantial evidence from proof of quid pro quo.
insights.quote: That doesn’t demonstrate corruption, but it is exactly how a highly localized legislative earmark can pass with effectively zero scrutiny.

insights.claim: Tailored grant eligibility can be classified as a benign geographic set-aside, a de facto earmark, or a quid pro quo payoff, with the latter requiring evidence of motive or communications.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Useful taxonomy for evaluating regulatory favoritism claims.

themes.theme: AI as investigative tool and public choice method

insights.claim: ChatGPT was able to iteratively trace legislative history, IRS filings and political affiliations to build a network linking a grantee to budget legislators.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: LLMs lower the cost of investigative political-economy research and transparency scrutiny.
insights.locator: I decided to investigate with ChatGPT

insights.claim: Most public choice economics is not done as micro-history of specific deals because economists prefer models and see such work as journalism or history.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Suggests an underexploited research niche, potentially opened up by AI-assisted archival work.
insights.quote: I suppose economists like models and consider this sort of thing journalism or history at best.
